title: The Extraction of Vienna
premise: Bram Nakamura has spent six years as a ghost: a private security contractor whose real name, real face, and real past are buried under three layers of forged identity. When a luxury listing goes live featuring photographs of her current safe house — taken from inside, while she was on rotation — she realizes someone sold her location, and the only person who could have is the handler who recruited her. Following the thread through Vienna's auction houses, embassy back channels, and a border town where checkpoints change shifts at dawn, Bram uncovers an inheritance scheme built on stolen identities, including her own. To survive, she must trade her invisibility for the truth, outmaneuver a patient assassin named Corvin, and decide whether belonging to anyone is worth being findable. The story ends at the shifting checkpoint, where Bram hands over the evidence that dismantles the scheme, lets her old identity die officially, and crosses into a life she chooses rather than one she hides in.
about_author: Ines Reyes is a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients she was never allowed to name. She writes thrillers about people whose survival depends on being forgotten.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Scrolling property sites during a sleepless night shift, Bram finds her safe house listed with interior photos — her kettle, her books, the dent in the wall from a bad night. The emotional beat is cold vertigo: the illusion of safety collapsing in a single image.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Rules
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. She runs her protocols: burn the house, move, vanish. But the photos include a shot of her own shoulder and laptop, meaning the seller watched her recently. Flashback establishes her fabricated identity and the handler, Marek, who built it. Beat: discipline cracking into fear.

chapters.title: Marek Doesn't Answer
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. She flies to Vienna to confront Marek and finds his office emptied, his number reassigned to a florist. A colleague mentions Marek liquidated everything ten days ago. Beat: the ground tilting — the man who made her invisible has made himself invisible first.

chapters.title: Corvin Waits Well
chapters.summary: Assassin Corvin's POV. Introduced watching Bram's hotel from a café, methodical and almost affectionate about his craft. He isn't ordered to kill her yet; he's told to confirm she saw the listing. Beat: quiet menace, the reader learns she's already being managed.

chapters.title: The Photograph Provenance
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. She traces the listing to a boutique agency tied to an estate liquidation firm — and to a probate file bearing her birth name, Nakamura, which no living record should contain. Beat: fury braided with grief; her buried past is surfacing without her consent.

chapters.title: What Her Father Signed
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, interleaved with document excerpts. In a Viennese archive she finds her father's estate papers: he didn't die intestate as she believed. Someone has been administering his assets for twenty years — using her identity as the heir of record. Beat: inheritance revealed as theft.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One File
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A consular officer, Ilse Brandt, notices the same probate anomaly and opens a quiet inquiry; meanwhile a domestic intelligence liaison flags Bram as a person of interest. Beat: converging pressure — Bram is now hunted by paperwork as much as by people.

chapters.title: The Florist Knows Flowers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The florist with Marek's old number agrees to talk for cash: Marek visited weekly, always sending white lilies to a name Bram recognizes — her mother's maiden name. Beat: dread deepening into personal violation; the conspiracy has been courting her dead family.

chapters.title: Safe House Two
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. She improvises a bolt hole in a boarding house run by Yusuf, an observant, unimpressed landlord who sees more than he says. First human warmth in years. Beat: tentative belonging — dangerous for someone whose survival depends on detachment.

chapters.title: Corvin Makes Contact
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Corvin sits down across from Bram in a museum café, courteous, and offers her a choice: walk away and live, or keep digging and force his hand. He reveals he was hired not to kill her but to keep her alive until the estate settles. Beat: the trap has velvet lining.

chapters.title: The Beneficiary
chapters.summary: Ilse Brandt's POV. Ilse identifies the estate's co-beneficiary: a shell trust administered through a law firm with ties to a former intelligence contractor — Marek's original employer. Beat: scale revealed; this is institutional, not personal greed alone.

chapters.title: Rotation
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Her security firm orders her onto a protection detail in Bratislava — a job arranged, she suspects, to keep her moving. On the assignment she protects a client who reminds her of her younger self. Beat: mirror moment; what she guards versus what guards her.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Studying the border checkpoint near the archive town, she maps the shift changes: ninety minutes each dawn when records sync imperfectly between systems. She begins planning to move the probate file physically. Beat: hope with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Yusuf's Question
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Yusuf asks why she never unpacks. Cornered by kindness, Bram tells him a partial truth — that she inherited nothing but debts and a name worth killing for. Beat: vulnerability as turning point; being known feels like both wound and armor.

chapters.title: Marek Found
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following the lilies, Bram finds Marek in a care facility outside Graz, early-stage dementia, lucid in windows. He confesses he sold her location to settle a debt to the trust — and gives her the key to a deposit box before losing the thread. Beat: betrayal and pity entangled.

chapters.title: The Deposit Box
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The box holds her father's original will, proof the trust's administration was fraudulent, and a letter her father wrote to the daughter he thought would come looking. Beat: grief detonating quietly; the inheritance was never money — it was being claimed.

chapters.title: Corvin's Contract Changes
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. His employer amends the contract: terminate once the box is recovered. Corvin, who respects craft and dislikes sloppy orders, hesitates — then warns Bram obliquely through a dead-drop note. Beat: the assassin acquires a conscience, or at least a preference.

chapters.title: Ilse Offers a Deal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ilse corners Bram with what her agencies know and offers immunity-shaped cooperation: hand over the documents, testify quietly, disappear again. Bram counters — she wants the fraud prosecuted publicly, her name restored, not sealed away. Beat: negotiation over what justice costs.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Climax begins: Bram moves the file through the checkpoint town during shift change, using the firm's own protection protocols against its client. Corvin intercepts her at the crossing — and instead of killing her, walks beside her through the gap, settling his account. Beat: adrenaline sharpened into strange alliance.

chapters.title: What the Trust Buried
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. With the originals authenticated, the trust unravels: arrests at the law firm, Marek's employer exposed, the listing traced to a panicked asset manager. Bram testifies under a negotiated arrangement. Beat: vindication arriving without triumph — institutions absorb even their exposure.

chapters.title: The Name on the Door
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Falling action: Bram legally reclaims her identity, visits her father's grave with the letter, and formally resigns from the firm. Yusuf offers her the boarding house's vacant room, no questions asked. Beat: mourning completed; identity chosen rather than assumed.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, final scene echoing chapter thirteen. At dawn, Bram crosses the checkpoint openly, passport in her true name, watching the new shift take over behind her. Corvin, retired somewhere warm, reads about the trial. Beat: resolution — she stops being invisible and starts being present.
